claims.statement: agent/dashboard/options.py is the single registry of selectable models: SUPPORTED_MODELS is a hand-maintained list of ModelOption records (provider-prefixed id, label, per-model efforts list, default_effort, supports_images), and SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS is the frozen set every resolution layer checks membership against.

The efforts a model accepts are per-model and non-uniform (for example Kimi K3 only accepts low/high/max and Gemini has minimal through high), and model_supports_effort/model_supports_images validate a stored selection against the model's own ModelOption fields.

Deprecated model ids are not canonically replaced: DEPRECATED_MODEL_REPLACEMENTS has empty values and canonical_model_pair always returns None. Deprecated ids are excluded from provider_fallback_pair and defer to defaults, while unsupported non-deprecated ids may use same-provider and, where possible, same-Claude-family fallback.

default_model_pair() is the deployment-level terminal fallback: it reads LLM_MODEL_ID and LLM_REASONING_EFFORT, validates that the resulting model is supported and default-eligible, and raises ValueError for an unsupported model or effort.

For a hosted agent run, build_agent seeds workspace main/subagent and routing defaults, applies a profile only when no stored thread model exists, then uses stored thread settings when present; a valid explicit configurable agent_model_id/agent_effort replaces main and subagent choices and the resolved settings are persisted back to the thread.

Dashboard thread creation resolves a model pair in workspace-default, valid-profile, valid-request order, but a deprecated request intentionally leaves the workspace pair rather than applying the profile/request; it then applies the Fable gate.

Workspace default resolution routes candidates through _resolve_default_pair, which returns a valid supported/default-eligible pair, otherwise a same-provider fallback, otherwise default_model_pair(), guaranteeing a constructible default despite stale or unknown stored settings.

The legacy instance settings record remains keyed 'default' in the ['team_settings'] namespace, while sparse workspace-specific overrides are stored in ['workspace_settings'] by slug; effective settings merge hardcoded defaults, instance fields, and workspace fields and fail soft to defaults on a store error.

WorkspaceSettings resolves distinct defaults per role (agent, reviewer, chat), where chat inherits the agent default when no chat-specific pair is usable; it also resolves separate subagent pairs, adaptive-routing tiers, and a title-model pair that can fall back to Anthropic on an Anthropic-only deployment.

Per-user profiles live in the ['profiles'] namespace holding a default model/effort, optional subagent pair, repository/branch and PR preferences, and adaptive-routing preference; profile-editable settings are split from encrypted GitHub OAuth tokens in ['oauth_tokens'] so profile saves and token refreshes cannot clobber one another.

On the run-start path profiles are read fail-soft (agent_overrides.load_profile logs and returns None so a store blip costs only per-user overrides), whereas dashboard reads use profiles.get_profile so failures surface.

normalize_profile_overrides accepts a profile's default_model/reasoning_effort only when the pair is valid and default-eligible, otherwise falls back to the same-provider pair for an unsupported id, and returns (None, None) for an absent, deprecated, or unknown-provider selection so the workspace default applies.

provider_model_kwargs translates a resolved effort string into provider-specific kwargs by dispatching on the model id prefix: OpenAI gets a reasoning dict, Anthropic gets adaptive/summarized thinking plus effort, Gemini 3+ gets thinking_level, Fireworks gets model_kwargs.reasoning_effort, and Baseten gets reasoning_effort for low/high/max.

make_model builds a chat model via init_chat_model and applies a default max_retries of 6 and a 600-second per-request timeout for known provider prefixes so a stalled provider connection becomes a retry instead of a wedged run.

make_model configures OpenAI models for the Responses API with store=false, output_version responses/v1, and include reasoning.encrypted_content, and uses desktop OpenAI OAuth when no OPENAI_API_KEY is set and the gateway is not applied.
make_model routes Baseten as an OpenAI-compatible provider and, when the gateway is disabled, requires BASETEN_API_KEY and points at the Baseten base URL, raising if the key is missing.

Gateway routing is tri-state: resolve_gateway_enabled treats a workspace gateway_enabled of True/False as authoritative and None as inheriting the deployment default, which is LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_ENABLED when set or a dedicated gateway key otherwise; when enabled, gateway_overrides supplies base_url/api_key and OpenAI Responses selection over direct-provider defaults.

fallback_model_id_for returns a cross-provider fallback (Anthropic primaries to OpenAI and vice versa) and None for Google/local/self-hosted providers; the run factory wires this into ModelFallbackMiddleware and honors an LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID environment override first.

Fable models are gated workspace-wide: disabling Fable swaps Fable defaults to a non-Fable Anthropic fallback, build_agent gates main, subagent, and title choices after snapshot resolution, and the workspace-aware options endpoint removes Fable choices and gates returned defaults.

Per-repository custom instructions are records stored in the ['agent_instructions'] namespace keyed by owner/name; the factory resolves them for the effective repository on a thread without a model snapshot, persists them in thread settings, and renders them into the shared system prompt as Repository-specific Custom Instructions.

Per-user custom instructions live in their own ['user_instructions'] namespace keyed by GitHub login and capped at 20,000 chars precisely because the dashboard Profile endpoint and the agent's save_user_instructions tool can both write them without clobbering profile fields.

During prepare-run, each participant's current personal instructions are loaded into that person's dynamic context block; the system prompt identifies the sender from the input-message envelope and says standing instructions apply only when acting on that person's requests, rather than making them shared thread instructions.

Instruction conflicts resolve in a strict order AGENTS.md > repository custom instructions > workspace instructions and default behavior; personal standing instructions yield to repository instructions and AGENTS.md and cannot be carried between participants.
For dashboard image-bearing run creation, a text-only resolved model is replaced with default_vision_model_pair; direct image-content validation rejects a missing or text-only model with HTTP 422.

Thread settings are a five-minute-cached typed agent_settings metadata snapshot containing model, subagent, routing, and repository-instruction fields; strict validation turns malformed metadata into an empty snapshot, and failed loads or writes are logged without aborting a run.

A profile boolean model_routing_enabled overrides the workspace routing toggle while None inherits it; routing pairs are stored on the thread, dashboard model_selection can choose auto or explicit, and /oswe question runs disable adaptive routing.
